question:
I have a very stupid question about templating in dbt.

I want to run a model tableC against uat-az , but only certain source tables of the model can be found in uat-az therefore, I want to exclude it from the sources.yml depending on target env.

Example :

I want to run the following :

dbt run --select tableX --target uat-az

(TableX is referencing TableC and other tables not shown here)

But had to make changes to the source.yml :

- name: sourceA
  schema: schemaA
  database: |
    {%- if "prod" in target.name  -%} raw_db_prod
    {%- else -%} raw_db_uat
    {%- endif -%}
  tables:
  - name: tableA
    description: The table A.
    freshness:
      warn_after: {count: 12, period: hour}
      error_after: {count: 24, period: hour}
    loaded_at_field: "to_timestamp(json:dt::string)"
    columns:
    - name: json
      description:  json.
- name: tableB
    description: The table B.
    columns:
    - name: dt
      description: the dt
    - name: sn
      description: the sn
    - name: payload

    {%- if target.name != "uat-az" and target.name != "prod-az" %}
  
- name: tableC
    description: The table C.
    columns:

    - name: _file
      description: the _file.
    - name: _line
      description: the _line.
     
    {% endif -%}

I have tried many different configurations for including different identation, spacing handling, etc. :

{%- if target.name != "uat-az" and target.name != "prod-az" %}
{% endif -%}
{%- if target.name != "uat-az" and target.name != "prod-az" -%}
{%- endif -%}

yml files are very strict in terms of indentation and I am getting confused with the documentation: https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/templates/#whitespace-control

List of envs :

  • prod = main prod
  • uat = maint uat
  • prod-az = new uat
  • uat-az = new uat

Is there a special syntax in the context of yml files ? What is it I am doing wrong ?
title: Using 'if' statement with Jinja templating in a yml file
answer:
If I get your question correctly, you're trying to hide some sources based on your target. I don't think it's possible thing to do via YAML config.

What is possible though is to exclude non-prod sources from the code of your target model. For example, it can look like this:

SELECT col1, col2, col3
FROM <table_that_exists_in_every_target>
{%- if "prod" in target.name -%}
UNION
SELECT col1, col2, col3
FROM <table_that_exists_ONLY_IN_PROD>
{%- endif -%}
